You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The unemployment rate of 7.7% with a fed funds rate near 0.17% points to early 2013. Unemployment was 7.9% in January 2013 and 7.7% in February 2013, so the date is probably February or March.

Other figures fit this window:
- The 10-year yield of 1.73% matches February 2013, when it was about 1.88%. In January it was about 1.91%.
- Gold's 3-month return of -6%, with a 1-month return of -3.1%, fits February 2013, when gold fell.
- The VIX at 22.7 is above its roughly 14 level in February. It was elevated in late February because of the Italian election, though the month-end level was about 15.5, so the figure looks off for that month.
- CPI of 1.77% YoY matches January 2013 (1.6%) or February (2.0%).

The 12-month change in unemployment of -1.0 points fits a rate of 7.7% against 8.7% a year earlier. Counting back, the rate was 8.2% in February 2012, which is not consistent with that. A different reading is that 7.7% is the November 2012 value, down from 8.7% in November 2011, and that would fit the 12-month change exactly. The 3-month change of -0.4 also fits, since August 2012 was 8.1%.

So the snapshot is probably November 2012:
- The 10-year yield was about 1.6-1.7%.
- The VIX was about 18-20 in mid-November, so 22.7 is a bit high.
- Gold at about 1,720 had fallen over the month.
- Emerging-market equity returned +6.7% over 1 month, which does not fit November, when it was about +1%. That fits better with October-November 2012 or with September 2012.

Equity returns could still match February 2013 if the snapshot used a different data vintage, but the unemployment path fits November 2012 better. Counting back from 7.7%, with a 3-month change of -0.4 and the unemployment rate in August at 8.1%, the date is likely November 2012 or close to it. Developed ex-US equity returned +6.3% over 3 months, which is plausible for Sep-Nov. A VIX of 22.7 is plausible for the 2012 election and fiscal-cliff period.
